findings.text: Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static credential called an internal connection API token.
findings.quote: Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static credential called an internal connection API token. They’re ideal for custom automations and workflows — things like syncing data, sending notifications, or building internal dashboards.

findings.text: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication.
findings.quote: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication. At creation time, you choose their installation scope: Any workspace (any Notion user can install; Marketplace-eligible) or Selected workspaces only (restricted to workspaces you select; not Marketplace-eligible).

findings.text: Personal access tokens are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, Workers, and tools that should act as one Notion user.
findings.quote: Personal access tokens (PATs) are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, Workers, and tools that should act as one Notion user. A PAT uses the creator’s workspace membership and page permissions.

findings.text: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.
findings.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace. You can create and use a public connection without listing it.

findings.text: You are required to be a workspace owner to create an internal connection.
findings.quote: You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.

findings.text: Navigate to the Developer portal to create a new public connection.
findings.quote: Navigate to the Developer portal and create a new public connection.

findings.text: Fill out the connection details including redirect URIs and installation scope.
findings.quote: Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section and the connection’s installation scope — either Any workspace or Selected workspaces only.

findings.text: Direct the user to the authorization URL to start the OAuth flow.

findings.text: If a page is not shared with the connection, API requests will return an error.
findings.quote: Once the connection is shared, you can start making API requests. If the page is not shared, any API requests made will respond with an error.

findings.text: Business and Enterprise plans have a per-connection rate limit of 600 requests per minute.
findings.quote:
Business and Enterprise

findings.text: All other plans have a per-connection rate limit of 180 requests per minute.

findings.text: Querying a data source has a limit of about 3 requests per second per connection.
findings.quote: Querying a data source has a separate limit of about 3 requests per second per connection.

findings.text: Payloads have a maximum size of 1000 block elements.
findings.quote: Note that in addition to the property limits below, payloads have a maximum size of 1000 block elements and 500KB overall.

findings.quote: Do not retry every error. Retry 429 and 529 responses, except a 429 with public_api_request_blocked.

findings.text: Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static credential called an internal connection API token.
findings.quote: Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static credential called an internal connection API token. They’re ideal for custom automations and workflows — things like syncing data, sending notifications, or building internal dashboards.

findings.text: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication and are intended for apps used by many Notion users or workspaces.
findings.quote: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 for authentication. At creation time, you choose their installation scope: Any workspace (any Notion user can install; Marketplace-eligible) or Selected workspaces only (restricted to workspaces you select; not Marketplace-eligible).

findings.text: Personal access tokens are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, and tools that act as one Notion user.
findings.quote: Personal access tokens (PATs) are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, Workers, and tools that should act as one Notion user. A PAT uses the creator’s workspace membership and page permissions.

findings.text: The fastest way to start building is the Quickstart, which involves creating a personal access token.
findings.quote: The fastest way to start building is the Quickstart — create a personal access token, make your first API request, and see a new page appear in your workspace in under two minutes.

findings.text: Use a PAT for scripts or tools acting as you, an internal connection for team-owned automations, or a public connection for apps other users install.
findings.quote: Use a PAT when a script, CLI workflow, Worker, or trusted tool should act as you. Use an internal connection for team-owned workspace automations, or a public connection when other Notion users need to install your app.

findings.text: Public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Notion Marketplace.
findings.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Marketplace.

findings.text: Internal connections and public connections restricted to specific workspaces are not eligible for the Marketplace.
findings.quote: Internal connections and Selected workspaces only public connections are not eligible.

findings.text: Public connections can be used via OAuth without being listed on the Marketplace.
findings.quote: Public connections work independently of Marketplace listings. Listing on the Marketplace is optional and helps your connection reach a wider audience, but your connection can be used via its OAuth flow without being listed.
